newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent, gas oil seen weaker after bearish APIs.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent, gas oil seen weaker after bearish APIs.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil are expected to open weaker on Wednesday, catching up with losses on U.S. markets posted in anticipation of bearish weekly stocks data from the American Petroleum Institute (API), brokers said.
April gas oil, which settled at $165.50 a tonne, was expected to begin trading about $1 lower. May Brent was due to open 10-15 cents a barrel lower after settling at $19.11 in London.
"This week NYMEX is open for an hour after Brent and it was sold off in anticipation of the bearish APIs after London shut," said a broker.
API figures released after the markets closed showed a rise in U.S. crude stocks of 6.4 million barrels last week, exceeding many traders expectations.
Crude oil inventories nationwide were pegged at 308.9 million barrels for the week ended March 28, up 11.4 million barrels compared to the same week last year.
Refined product data was seen as broadly neutral, although some brokers said a 2.58 million barrel fall in distillate stocks, and firmer European sentiment, could support gas oil.
"Gas oil could open as much as $1.50 lower but we don't see it making that given the support in Europe," said a broker.
But dealers saw little support in gasoline markets. U.S. gasoline inventories were drawn down by a modest 335,000 barrels, amid high production levels and lacklustre demand.

Reports that Iraq wants to double oil exports from $2 billion to $4 billion under the U.N. oil-for-food deal, due for renewal in June, were ignored. Diplomats expressed severe doubt that any bid to increase sales would gain U.N. approval.
Meanwhile, weak cash and physical crude markets in Europe would continue to weigh heavily on Brent, brokers added.
